column1: # iormesh agent hook table, variant jdk17 (JDK 17 to 20; checked on 17 —
# GraalVM CE 17.0.9, a HotSpot JDK — while 18 to 20 are assumed to match).
# Where 17 differs from the jdk21 variant (decision #29): file channels
# go through sun/nio/ch/FileDispatcherImpl (no UnixFileDispatcherImpl);
# socket writes and closes call FileDispatcherImpl's natives from
# SocketDispatcher (no UnixDispatcher); FileDispatcherImpl.close reaches
# FileDescriptor.close, already hooked; RandomAccessFile's readBytes and
# writeBytes are themselves native, so read/write are hooked; Net's
# socket factories take a "reuse" flag; UnixNativeDispatcher has
# stat(UnixPath) instead of stat2.
# Written by hand from javap -p -s of the JDK classes and checked against
# the running JDK by `mage agentTest` (HookTableTest.matchesRunningJdk).
# One row per hooked Java method (overloads are separate rows). Columns,
# tab-separated:
#   id        hook id the rewritten method passes to Hooks.enter/exit
#             (unique in this file, 1..; ids are per variant, the agent
#             reports the table it used)
#   kind      the I/O the bracket stands for (open, read, write, close,
#             seek, socket, bind, connect, listen, accept, shutdown,
#             unlink, rename, stat)
#   class     internal name of the class whose method body is rewritten
#   method    method name
#   desc      method descriptor
#   native    the JNI native the body calls (same class unless qualified
#             as owner.name) — the tracer's uprobe for this hook
#   syscalls  the syscall kinds allowed under that native; anything else
#             inside the bracket is JVM work (S1)
